# Exact whole-integral compensation for the sextic brother

STATUS: ANALYTIC_PAPER_CANDIDATE; independent review pending.
Base: f0237d451168eb59a01fe19ec018462ed1bf460b.
ORIGINAL_THETA_V and RH: OPEN. No original negative witness.

## T0. Return point and decision

The fixed positive raw-response norm floor is excluded for the theta source.
The quartic source already has a direct Gram map, but its separate cancellation
layers are positive. This worked comparison addresses the harder geometry:
can a source have negative cancellation layers, no positive raw point-response
floor, and nevertheless an EXACT positive representation of the WHOLE V?

Yes, for the separately identified source f6(t)=exp(-t^6). Its Fourier
real-zero theorem was already proved in RECONSTRUCTION_CLASS_OBSTRUCTION R4;
it is not a new discovery. Here an explicit square-sum of Fourier TAILS
accounts for the entire integral and its boundary. It is derived without
taking a positive square root of V6. This is a worked compensation control,
not a new source identity for theta or a new RH criterion. In particular it
does not supply the unproved real-zero input for the actual theta transform.

Reconciled inputs: LAYER_GRAM_TEST L1--L9; RECONSTRUCTION_CLASS_OBSTRUCTION
R4 (the already positive sextic Fourier sibling); RAW_RESPONSE_FLOOR F3--F5;
SOURCE_GENERATOR_SUPPORT_AUDIT A2--A13; DIRECT_PICK_BRIDGE's already unpaid
real-negative-zero input on the actual normalized Mellin function H. This
uses a partial-fraction decomposition of the old Fourier multiplier iF'/F
WHEN its real-zero input is independently known, followed by a separate
tail-field realization. No unitary equivalence between the old full-line
generator and the discrete diagonal field operator is claimed or needed.
This is not a replacement for the old SUPPORT question.

## T1. The independent input for this OTHER source

For this note only, define

 f(t)=exp(-t^6), F(z)=int_R exp(-izt)f(t)dt,
 V6(x,y)=int_0^infinity (2t+x+y)f(t+x)f(t+y)dt.

This f is not Phi, not a truncation of Phi, and has no claimed prime-product
or modular source identity. Positive normalization rescales V6 harmlessly.
All real nodes and all finite complex coefficient rows are considered.

For rho(s)=exp(-s^3), direct Gamma integration and triplication give

 D6(u)=(1/3)Gamma((u+1/2)/3),
 H6(u)=D6(u)/Gamma(u+1/2)
      =2pi*3^(-u-1)/[Gamma(u/3+1/2)Gamma(u/3+5/6)].       (T1)

The last expression is entire of order at most one, positive on u>=0,
and has only negative real zeros. The classical Laguerre coefficient
theorem, already checked in the pinned primary Baricz--Singh, Lemma 1,
printed p.2, applies: an entire real function of order less than two with
only negative real zeros has an exponential coefficient transform with
only negative real zeros. The exact moment identity is

 F(z)=sqrt(pi) sum_(n>=0) H6(n)(-z^2/4)^n/n!.            (T2)

Thus F has only real zeros, with multiplicities allowed. Dominating by
exp(R|t|-t^6) pays every compact z-set. Young's inequality also gives
|F(z)|<=C exp(C'|z|^(6/5)), hence order at most 6/5<2.
F is even, real on the real axis, and F(0)>0. Its real zeros can therefore
be listed as pairs +/-gamma, gamma>0, each counted with its multiplicity,
and Hadamard factorization gives

 F(z)=F(0) product_(gamma>0)(1-z^2/gamma^2),
 sum_(gamma>0) gamma^(-2)<infinity,
 F'(z)/F(z)=sum_(gamma>0)[1/(z-gamma)+1/(z+gamma)].       (T3)

Evenness removes a linear exponential factor and order less than two
excludes a quadratic one. All products and logarithmic derivatives in T3
converge locally uniformly away from the zeros. No assertion of simple
zeros, explicit zero positions, or positive matrices is used here.

## T2. A field constructed by tails, with estimates at BOTH ends

For each signed zero gamma define the scalar tail

 T_gamma(t)=int_0^infinity exp(i gamma s) f(t+s)ds.       (T4)

Because F(-gamma)=0, this is ALSO

 T_gamma(t)=-int_(-infinity)^0 exp(i gamma s)f(t+s)ds.   (T5)

The equality is what pays the negative-t endpoint; discarding it would
give an incorrect integrability assertion for a generic frequency.
Differentiating, or integrating once by parts, yields exactly

 T_gamma'(t)=-f(t)-i gamma T_gamma(t).                  (T6)

Put

 A1(t)=|f(t)|+min(int_(-infinity)^t |f'(v)|dv,
                 int_t^infinity |f'(v)|dv),
 A2(t)=|f'(t)|+min(int_(-infinity)^t |f''(v)|dv,
                  int_t^infinity |f''(v)|dv).

Both are integrable with every polynomial weight, and decay rapidly at
both ends. One integration by parts in either T4 or T5, then choosing
the smaller tail, proves

 |T_gamma(t)|<=A1(t)/|gamma|.                           (T7)

Two integrations by parts cancel the leading terms in opposite frequencies:

 |T_gamma(t)+T_(-gamma)(t)|<=2 A2(t)/gamma^2.            (T8)

All derivatives of f have the required rapid decay. These estimates use
actual zero frequencies and hold with constants independent of gamma.
In particular each tail is in L1 and L2, and the paired series of T8
converges in weighted L1 for every polynomial weight.

## T3. Exact reconstruction of t f(t), not an assumed energy law

Use the Fourier convention of T1. Equation T6 gives

 hat(T_gamma)(omega)=i F(omega)/(omega+gamma),           (T9)

with its removable value at omega=-gamma. Fourier transforms of the paired
series can be taken termwise by T8 and summability in T3. At real omega
away from the zeros, T3 identifies their sum with i F'(omega). Fourier
uniqueness in L1 then proves, everywhere by continuity,

 t f(t)=sum_(gamma>0)[T_gamma(t)+T_(-gamma)(t)].         (T10)

The summation is paired. We never assert absolute summability of the
UNPAIRED scalar T_gamma series. Equation T10 reconstructs the same flux
factor t f(t), not a surrogate with a chosen normalization.

## T4. The whole original-form integral is a sum of squares

For real x,y, T6 and real gamma give

 -d/dt[conj(T_gamma(t+x)) T_gamma(t+y)]
   =f(t+x)T_gamma(t+y)+conj(T_gamma(t+x))f(t+y).         (T11)

Integrate over the FULL physical half-line. The boundary at infinity is
zero by T7; the boundary at t=0 is retained. Sum finite symmetric sets
of zero pairs, then take their limit using T8 for the integrated flux.
The resulting boundary series is absolutely convergent by T7 and T3.
With T10, the exact identity is

 V6(x,y)=sum_(gamma signed) conj(T_gamma(x))T_gamma(y).
                                                               (T12)
Thus Psi_x=(T_gamma(x)) belongs to ell2 of the zero multiset, and

 V6[c]=sum_(gamma signed)|sum_i c_i T_gamma(x_i)|^2>=0  (T13)

for EVERY finite complex row, with arbitrary real shifts. Cauchy--Schwarz
or T7 pays mixed sums; no rank restriction or discarded cutoff term occurs.
Repeated zeros mean repeated equal coordinates, i.e. their correct positive
multiplicity. T11 proves that the sign arises from the COMPLETE flux and
its boundary, not from positivity of its separate integral pieces.

## T5. This SAME positive example has negative cancellation layers

Apply the old exact cancellation variable, now to f6:

 m=(x+y)/2, d=(x-y)/2,
 K_s(x,y)=f(sqrt(s+m^2)+d)f(sqrt(s+m^2)-d),
 V6(x,y)=int_0^infinity K_s(x,y)ds.                    (T14)

For x,y>0, K_0=f(x)f(y). Normalize W_s=K_s/(f(x)f(y)).
The old exact tangent calculation, with q=f'/f=-6x^5, gives

 J(x,y)=partial_s W_s|_0=(q(x)+q(y))/(x+y)
       =-6(x^4-x^3y+x^2y^2-xy^3+y^4),
 C(x,y)=partial_x partial_y J=18x^2-24xy+18y^2.         (T15)

For any distinct positive a,b, C(a,a)=12a^2, C(b,b)=12b^2,
C(a,b)=12ab+18(a-b)^2, and

 det C_{a,b}=-108(a-b)^2(3a^2-2ab+3b^2)<0.            (T16)

Choose v=(-C(a,b)/C(a,a),1), so v^T C v<0. Replace each derivative
evaluation at a,b by a sufficiently small forward difference. The combined
four-node functional z_epsilon has coefficient sum zero, and
z_epsilon^T J z_epsilon tends to v^T C v<0. Fix a small epsilon BEFORE
taking s down to zero. Then

 z_epsilon^T W_s z_epsilon
    =s z_epsilon^T J z_epsilon+o(s)<0                  (T17)

for every sufficiently small s>0. Congruence by 1/f at these four nodes
returns an actual negative K_s row. The a,b and forward differences can
lie inside any prescribed open positive interval; simultaneous reflection
places them inside the original negative I. This uses a fixed finite row
for all sufficiently small s, not a different row at each layer.

Nevertheless T13 says its INTEGRATED V6 is nonnegative. Thus the exact
square-sum T12 actually reconciles the type of negative-layer obstruction
found for theta. It does not rely on a sibling whose layers were positive.

## T6. No raw point-response floor, yet a positive full energy

For this same f6, -f'/f=6t^5 on t>0. If R>0 and L_R=6R^5,
f(R+s)<=f(R)exp(-L_R s). Exact evenness gives

 0<V6(-R,-R)/f(-R)^2
   <=R/L_R+1/(2L_R^2) ->0.                            (T18)

Both V6 and f(x)f(y) extend holomorphically to C x C (sextic decay is
uniform for bounded complex shifts). The already accepted all-rank analytic
propagation lemma therefore excludes V6>=kappa f(x)f(y) on all finite
rows of any open interval, for every kappa>0. This is only the point
measure delta_0 comparison, not the entire theta F1 weight class.

Consequently Psi_x in T12 cannot have a bounded linear scalar readout
returning f(x). This is fully compatible with T6: taking a derivative
of a selected tail coordinate is not a bounded scalar observation of the
pointwise ell2 vector Psi_x. No closability or domain claim for such a
derivative is needed. The explicit energy exists despite the excluded floor.

## T6a. An explicit space in which the singular input is well defined

There are infinitely many signed zeros: otherwise T3 would make F a
polynomial, contradicting its real-axis decay and F(0)>0. Define

 H=ell2(gamma),
 H_-1={v:sum_gamma |v_gamma|^2/(1+gamma^2)<infinity},
 b=(1)_gamma, A:H->H_-1, (Az)_gamma=-i gamma z_gamma.

Then b belongs to H_-1 by T3, and A is bounded between the stated spaces.
The Fourier transform of f' also vanishes at every signed zero. Applying
the same two-end estimate to f' gives

 |T_gamma'(x)|<=A2(x)/|gamma|.

This bound is uniform on compact real x-intervals. Finite truncations and
their derivatives converge uniformly there in H, so x->Psi_x is C1 into H.
The coordinate equations T6 therefore give an actual vector identity

 Psi'_x=A Psi_x-b f(x) in H_-1.                        (T19)

Two integrations by parts also show gamma T_gamma(x)->i f(x)!=0 as
|gamma|->infinity. Thus Psi_x is NOT in the H-domain of diag(gamma),
which requires sum gamma^2|T_gamma(x)|^2<infinity. The two terms on
the right of T19 separately fail to lie in H, but their difference does
lie in H and equals Psi'_x. This is explicit cancellation in a larger
space, with the positive energy still measured in H. It does not assert
an ordinary H-domain generator equation, a bounded input in H, a closable
scalar readout, or a source-preserving construction for theta.

## T7. Mapping back to theta and exact stopping condition

For theta, the same candidate tails at known real zeros exist and obey
their first-order equations. The sum over ONLY known real zeros, however,
cannot be declared to reconstruct t f(t): T3 would require accounting
for ALL zeros of the actual F, and excluding nonreal zeros is RH. Assuming
T3 for actual F would insert the desired conclusion into the construction.

For f6 the entrance was instead paid by the explicit Gamma quotient T1
and the classical coefficient preserver T2. For theta the actual H is a
different entire function; the old DIRECT_PICK_BRIDGE leaves its negative
real-zero property open. Neither the Gamma triplication identity for H6,
source-tail bounds, negative-layer compensation nor the existence of a
skew-adjoint generator pays that property for actual H.

This is a worked all-rank compensation model, not a new unproved request
to build a reservoir or repeat SUPPORT/Pick. A source-specific entrance
remains necessary before applying this mechanism to original V. No new
Pro proof job, original sign result, negative theta row, canonical admission,
Lean certification, or source-sign counter reset follows.

AUTOPSY: dropped=OBJECT_IDENTITY; note=The exact spectral-tail square sum is proved for the independently real-zero sextic source; its real-zero entrance is unproved for the theta source and cannot be assumed in the transfer.

The complete argument, the added T6a/T19, and the final T0 correction were read. Final `SPECTRAL_TAIL_COMPENSATION_PINS.json`: SHA256 `5b464eb48666beaaeb536213298401e9aede3acbe12c8f8addcb911cad965e12`.

T1–T19 pass. This constructs an exact positive square-sum for the whole V6 of exp(-t^6), including all finite complex rows and the half-line boundary, while that same source has negative cancellation layers and no positive raw delta_0 floor. It also rigorously locates its singular input in H_-1. The theorem is only for the stated sextic control; no actual theta real-zero, SUPPORT, Pick, V-sign or RH assertion is accepted.

## 1. Source pins, named classical input and corrected relationship

All manifest input hashes were checked against the isolated research files:

`orchestrator/state/CHANNEL_RUNTIME.json` matches `f7bb8eed28bf9b67292f67bbbdde96cecb4baf42e758e0acbb4be34d5baa6418`; it is provenance, not a mathematical input or live dispatch authority. Relevant source formulas were read directly: reconstruction R4; layer L1–L9; raw-response comparison/readout; source-generator definitions and A8–A13 SUPPORT identification; direct-Pick R2–R3 and its open entrance. Previously accepted analytic propagation is inherited rather than represented as a new lemma.

The local Baricz–Singh authors' PDF has SHA256 `992a42316a41b39027377cbb2690b908ee14f3c1e2464b23c9727316d882abc7`; its text has SHA256 `3f09d27198002e3f9d8107cbc9422738b41e015c66ba9763fd8329398b8d2c69`. I reread Lemma 1, printed p.2. It is the classical Laguerre theorem for the exponential coefficient transform of a real entire function of order below two with negative real zeros. The theorem is an explicitly named external input, not independently reproved here. The earlier project proof already pays its sextic hypotheses. Standard Hadamard factorization is also used with its required growth conditions checked below.

The final T0 correction is important and accepted: the argument decomposes the old Fourier multiplier iF'/F into partial fractions, then constructs a separate tail-field realization. The full-line multiplication generator B and the discrete diagonal operator on the zero multiset have not been shown unitarily equivalent. Calling the construction the spectral decomposition of B itself would overstate the result; the final bytes no longer do so.

## 2. T1–T3: independent sextic entrance and paired product

Initially Re u>-1/2, substitution v=s^3 gives D6(u)=Gamma((u+1/2)/3)/3. Apply triplication with v=u/3+1/6 to Gamma(3v)=Gamma(u+1/2). Cancelling Gamma(v) gives exactly

    H6(u)=2pi 3^(-u-1)/[Gamma(u/3+1/2)Gamma(u/3+5/6)].

The reciprocal Gamma factors give an entire continuation of order at most one. Its zeros are the negative progressions -3n-3/2 and -3n-5/2; the exponential factor has no zeros. It is real on the real axis and positive for u>=0. These are independent of any zero-location premise about the original theta transform.

The even moments of exp(-t^6) equal D6(n). Inserting Gamma(n+1/2)=(2n)!sqrt(pi)/(4^n n!) into the Fourier moment expansion proves T2 with exactly the factor sqrt(pi) and argument -z^2/4. The Laguerre theorem applied to H6 gives negative real zeros of its exponential coefficient transform, whose value at zero is positive. Thus every Fourier zero is real; simplicity is unnecessary.

For every R, exp(R|t|-t^6) dominates the Fourier integrand and derivatives on |z|<=R. Young's inequality in the form R|t|<=t^6/2+C R^(6/5) gives the stated finite-order bound after integrating exp(-t^6/2). Hence order(F)<=6/5<2. Hadamard factorization therefore has at most a linear exponential factor and canonical genus at most one. Pairing the zeros gamma and -gamma cancels their genus-one exponentials; evenness removes the remaining linear exponential. F(0)>0 fixes the constant and excludes a zero at zero. This proves T3 and summability of gamma^-2, with multiplicity counted throughout.

The paired product and logarithmic derivative converge locally uniformly away from zeros. No quadratic exponential or unrecorded polynomial logarithmic-derivative term survives. A finite zero multiset would make F a polynomial, contradicting its real-axis Fourier decay and F(0)>0. Thus the infinitude later used in T6a is also justified.

## 3. T4–T8: both tails and uniform estimates

Substitution v=t+s gives the full oscillatory integral as exp(-i gamma t)F(-gamma). Its vanishing is exactly why the future integral equals minus the past integral. This is a property of a zero frequency, not a generic oscillation identity. It pays the negative-t endpoint as well as the positive one.

One integration by parts in the future integral gives

    T_gamma(t)=-f(t)/(i gamma)
               -(1/(i gamma)) integral_0^infinity exp(i gamma s)f'(t+s)ds.

The corresponding past formula has the same first term and the opposite sign on the derivative tail. Taking the better bound gives T7. Two integrations give the leading i f(t)/gamma term plus a remainder bounded by (|f'(t)| plus the selected f'' tail)/gamma^2. Adding opposite frequencies cancels the leading terms, yielding precisely T8 with factor 2.

All f derivatives are rapidly decreasing. At each end choose the tail extending toward that end; A1 and A2 then decay faster than every power and are integrable with every polynomial weight, as well as locally bounded and square integrable. Their bounds are independent of gamma. Since there is a zero-free neighborhood of frequency zero and sum gamma^-2 is finite, each coordinate belongs to L1 and L2, and the paired scalar series converges absolutely as a series of weighted L1 norms. It also converges uniformly on compact t-sets by T8. This does not prove or require absolute summability of the unpaired scalar series.

Differentiating the actual integral gives T6, with the sign -i gamma. For each fixed gamma the ODE also shows T_gamma' is integrable, so its Fourier differentiation has no unpaid boundary distribution.

## 4. T9–T10: reconstruction in the exact Fourier convention

Fourier-minus sends a derivative to i omega times the transform. Therefore T6 gives

    i(omega+gamma) hat(T_gamma)(omega)=-F(omega),
    hat(T_gamma)(omega)=iF(omega)/(omega+gamma).

The apparent pole is removable since F(-gamma)=0. Both sides are continuous there because T_gamma is in L1. No delta-supported homogeneous solution is introduced; the actual two-tail function has already been fixed.

T8 permits termwise Fourier transformation of the paired L1 sum. Away from the real zeros its transform is iF times the paired partial-fraction series, namely iF'. The two transforms extend continuously through the isolated zeros. Since Fourier-minus sends t f(t) to iF'(omega), L1 uniqueness proves T10 almost everywhere, then everywhere by the established continuity. Thus the flux factor is exactly t f(t), with no missing factor 2 or pi and no assumed positivity law.

## 5. T11–T13: complete boundary identity and all complex rows

Differentiating conjugate(T_gamma(t+x))T_gamma(t+y), the two imaginary-frequency terms cancel because gamma is real. The remaining derivative is minus the right side of T11. Integrating over t>=0 retains the product at t=0 and has zero terminal product by T7.

First sum only finitely many complete positive/negative zero pairs. Then use paired weighted L1 convergence to pass to the integrated flux. For fixed shifts, the other factor f(t+x) or f(t+y) is bounded, so L1 convergence suffices to control these integrals. The boundary series is absolutely convergent: each absolute product is at most A1(x)A1(y)/gamma^2. These are distinct convergence arguments, and neither requires an unpaired scalar sum to converge absolutely.

Using T10 in the two flux terms produces

    f(t+x)(t+y)f(t+y)+f(t+y)(t+x)f(t+x),

the full integrand (2t+x+y)f(t+x)f(t+y). This establishes exactly T12. The signed zero multiset gives the correct two coordinates for each positive zero and repeats them according to multiplicity. Each Psi_x belongs to ell2, and finite linearity plus Cauchy–Schwarz gives T13 for every finite complex row. No rank, reality-of-coefficients, or disjoint-support restriction appears. The proof keeps the whole physical half-line and its t=0 boundary; it is not a positive-square-root definition of an unknown-sign kernel.

## 6. T14–T17: negative layers for the very same source

Evenness supplies the old cancellation substitution T14 without a lost negative integration interval. At positive nodes, K_0=f(x)f(y), so normalizing by these strictly positive values is legitimate. With q=-6x^5, polynomial division gives the displayed J, and direct mixed differentiation gives C=18x^2-24xy+18y^2.

Its diagonal is 12a^2 and the off-diagonal is 12ab+18(a-b)^2. Expanding the two-by-two determinant gives exactly

    -108(a-b)^2(3a^2-2ab+3b^2),

strictly negative for distinct positive a,b. The chosen vector has quadratic value det(C)/C(a,a)<0.

Take the two forward derivative differences with coefficients from that vector. Their combined four-node functional has total coefficient zero. Applying it in both variables of the polynomial J converges to the negative C form. One can choose a,b and sufficiently small positive step so all four distinct nodes remain within any prescribed open positive interval. Fix that step before expanding W_s. Since W_0 is the all-ones kernel, its value on this zero-sum functional vanishes and the first derivative term is strictly negative. The finite fixed row therefore gives negativity for every sufficiently small s>0.

Congruence by inverse f values gives an actual K_s row, and simultaneous reflection preserves the layer kernel, placing the row in the original negative interval when desired. No derivative distribution is passed off as an admissible row, and no interchange of the finite-difference and layer limits is needed. T13 applies to this very row after integration, showing the claimed compatibility of negative layers and a positive whole form.

## 7. T18: no bounded raw point readout

The exact sextic logarithmic slope is 6t^5. For u>=R>0 it is at least 6R^5, so the same squared-tail integration gives

    V6(-R,-R)/f(-R)^2 <=1/(6R^4)+1/(72R^10) ->0.

For bounded complex shifts, the real part of (t+z)^6+(t+w)^6 has positive leading 2t^6 and uniformly lower-degree corrections. This pays joint entire continuation of V6 by integration, while f(z)f(w) is plainly entire. The inherited all-rank propagation lemma thus rules out a fixed positive delta_0 floor on any open interval. The conclusion is not extended to the larger theta measure class.

If a bounded scalar functional on the explicit ell2 field returned f(x), its norm bound would supply such a floor, contradicting this result. This excludes a bounded pointwise readout, not the already constructed Gram energy and not an unproved class of all unbounded observations. Evaluating a coordinate derivative along the curve x to Psi_x is a different operation.

## 8. T19: rigorous cancellation in H_-1, without an H-domain evolution claim

The full Fourier transform of f' vanishes at each signed zero as well. Applying the same future/past integration-by-parts estimate to f' gives |T_gamma'(x)|<=A2(x)/|gamma|. On compact x-intervals the tails of both the coordinate series and derivative series tend uniformly to zero in ell2. Hence finite truncations prove Psi is C1 as an H=ell2-valued function.

The vector b=(1) lies in H_-1 because sum (1+gamma^2)^-1 is finite. The diagonal map A:H to H_-1 is bounded: sum gamma^2|z_gamma|^2/(1+gamma^2)<=||z||_H^2. Thus all terms in T19 are defined in H_-1, and coordinate equality proves the vector identity there.

Two integrations by parts give gamma T_gamma(x)=i f(x)+O_x(1/|gamma|). Since there are infinitely many signed zeros and f(x)>0, neither A Psi_x nor b f(x) belongs to H, and Psi_x is not in the H-domain of diag(gamma). Their leading coordinate terms are both f(x); their difference is exactly the H-valued derivative Psi'_x. The statement therefore exhibits a real cancellation between two terms in a larger space, while the energy remains the ordinary nonnegative H norm.

No separate H inner product with these singular terms is justified by this observation. In particular the accepted energy identity was derived from finite coordinate balances and controlled paired limits, not by an invalid formal pairing with b. No unitary equivalence, H-bounded input, standard H-domain generator equation, scalar-readout closability, or extra control-system realization is asserted.

## 9. Exact acceptance boundary

This is a working compensation sibling with an independently paid real-zero entrance. The actual Gamma quotient H6 is explicitly different from the theta Mellin quotient H. The old direct-Pick bridge still leaves the needed actual-source real-negative-zero premise unpaid. Existence of the full-line skew-adjoint multiplier without RH does not provide the real-zero partial fractions needed for this construction. Summing tails at only known real theta zeros cannot be declared to reconstruct the complete t f(t).

The result adds a concrete positive representation and domain explanation for the sextic control, not a source-specific theta property, proof of SUPPORT/Pick, original negative V witness or RH proof. It does not launch a new reservoir request or change a source-sign counter. Only this assigned private review file was written; other files and foreign canonical HOLD were preserved. No descendants, external research, provider dispatch, numerical source scan, Lean run, canonical mutation, commit or publication was performed.
